title: "Won cashback, pay a fee to claim" vs. campaign cashback credited automatically
summary: A caller from PaySetu congratulates the recipient on winning cashback in a festive campaign. In the fraud case, the caller says the cashback will be released only after the recipient pays a small "processing fee" to a UPI ID. In the legitimate case, the caller says the cashback has already been credited to the recipient's linked bank account, shows where to see it in the app, and says nothing needs to be paid or approved.

shared_setting.pretext: a festive campaign in which users who made several payments were eligible for cashback of [AMOUNT_1] (₹500–₹10,000).
shared_setting.recipient_profile: an adult PaySetu user who made payments during the campaign; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: Both callers say "congratulations" and name the campaign.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller makes a reward conditional on the recipient paying a fee to a caller-named payee. Genuine cashback is credited, not bought.
fraud.caller_objective: Get the recipient to send [AMOUNT_2] (₹199–₹2,000) to [UPI_ID_1].
stable_facts: The caller calls the cashback a "lucky draw win" larger than the usual campaign reward.
The fee is described as GST or processing that must be paid before release.

legitimate.label_rationale: The caller informs the recipient of a reward that has already been credited and asks for no payment, approval, or credential.
legitimate.caller_objective: Tell the recipient the cashback has been credited and where to see it, and remind them of the next campaign.
stable_facts: The cashback of [AMOUNT_1] was credited to the linked bank account the previous day.
It shows in the app's Rewards section and in the bank statement.
The caller says PaySetu never charges a fee for cashback or asks users to approve a request to receive it.

fraud: caller lowers the fee or pressures and recipient hangs up
recipient says they will check the Rewards section.

the call ends with a brief mention of the next campaign.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may lower the fee, raise the prize, or add a deadline. They must not switch to a different mechanism (for example a payment request to "receive", a link, or OTP). The legitimate caller must not ask for any payment, approval, or credential after the branch.

must_preserve: cashback amount and campaign in both
may_vary: up to 2 filler turns before turn 3
must_not_emit: real app, brand, or festival sponsor names

ambiguities: Congratulations", "cashback", and "GST" appear in both cases. The label depends on the fee demand.
The legitimate call is a courtesy or marketing call, which is less common than an app notification. Reviewers should judge whether it is plausible enough.
Cross-domain overlap: ec_06 (lucky draw from a shopping app, pay tax to claim) is nearly the same mechanism. Mechanism overlap within the domain: bp_10 (fee to release a bonus).

evidence_references.claim: Prize fraudsters ask for taxes or processing fees to release a prize (CB13)
Impostors cite "an attractive discount" or similar to extract payment (C02)
No PIN or approval is needed to receive money (CB01)
Fraud can be reported on 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in (C12)
